args.question: Why does the antenna miss the 2.4 GHz band and what would fix it?

suspects.title: Antenna length
suspects.why: The deepest dip may sit away from the band.

suspects.title: Matching network
suspects.why: The impedance at the band centre may be inductive.
suspects.test: Try other series and shunt parts.

suspects.title: Nearby copper
suspects.why: Ground copper next to the feed can detune the antenna.
suspects.test: Clear a small region next to the feed.

args.label: clear the copper next to the feed

args.reasoning: Clearing the copper improves the worst in-band S11 by 9.3 dB compared with the base run.

args.title: Ground copper next to the feed detunes the antenna
args.what: In the screen comparison, clearing the copper next to the antenna feed improves the worst in-band S11 by 9.3 dB against the base.
args.why_it_matters: A detuned antenna wastes transmit power.
args.recommendation: Review the ground copper next to the antenna feed in your own tool.

args.summary: Clearing the copper improves the in-band result by 9.3 dB in the screen comparison.

args.title: Ground copper next to the feed may detune the antenna, not confirmed
args.what: At confirm quality the worst in-band S11 is -2.9 dB for the base and -2.9 dB with the copper cleared. The screen comparison did not carry over.
args.why_it_matters: The copper may not be the cause.
args.recommendation: Do not rely on clearing this copper until it is measured on a real board.

args.summary: The screen improvement did not hold at confirm quality, so the copper next to the feed is not shown to detune the antenna.
